item.title: PMs Are Winning, Engineers Are Plateauing: The Tech Job Market in Late 2026
item.description:
Lenny Rachitsky's late-2026 job market report: PM openings are up 75% from their low, while engineering openings have stalled.
Design and user research hit record lows, remote falls to 14% of roles, and the Bay Area now beats remote worldwide.
Guests weigh Indeed's rebound in senior AI roles, the rise of forward deployed engineers, and why openings aren't hires.

Written and voiced with AI (OpenRouter · heygen/heygen-voice-1-turbo:free).

item.title: Become a Cracked Marketer: The Marketing Engineer Method
item.description:
The Startup Ideas Podcast writes up Cody Schneider's Marketing Engineer Method: a coding agent set up to make and ship ads.
Give the agent data, write-only access and tools, then turn one URL into five static ads and a 30-second avatar video for about $5.
Guests add research on long contexts, the evaluator loop behind his quality gate, and the FTC's rule on AI-generated reviews.
Sources: - Become a Cracked Marketer, The Startup Ideas Podcast (SIP) 🧃 (@startupideaspod) (https://x.com/startupideaspod/status/2120222028108337379) - Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts, Nelson F. item.title: The Secret Behind Viral Product Launches
item.description:
Kyle Jeong of Browserbase, with Tereza of Factory, explains how viral product launches on X are planned.
His playbook: a scroll-stopping video, sharp copy, a story with a villain, friends, paid reach, partners, press and IRL events.
Guests add X's ranking weights, Paul Graham on recruiting users by hand, and the FTC's rules for disclosing paid posts.

item.title: How to Build a One-Person Million Dollar Agency with AI Agents
item.description:
The Boring Marketer sketches a one-person marketing agency for plumbing and HVAC shops, run by teams of AI agents.
His math: 20 clients on three tiers for about $85,000 a month, with agents that bring you only the decisions.
Guests add the services-as-software trend, how to build agents with checkpoints, and why AI must never do the cold calls.

item.title: A Practical Guide to Security in November 2026
item.description:
Jack Cable's X article A Practical Guide to Security in November 2026, after a chaotic few weeks of hacks and critical bugs.
His point: years-old best practices still work, from passkeys and secret scans to a 7-day minimum package age.
Binance lost 6.34 billion dollars via a compromised developer laptop; most of these steps can start today.
Source: A Practical Guide to Security in November 2026, Jack Cable (@jackhcable) (https://x.com/jackhcable/status/2117731409246978489)

item.title: Marketing Engineers: 100x More Experiments with AI agents
item.description:
Greg Isenberg's X article on the marketing engineer: part marketer, part builder, running AI agents.
His playbook: write the business "brain" first, connect the data, then add agents one at a time with guardrails in the tools.
Why it matters: the cost of a marketing experiment keeps collapsing, and whoever learns fastest wins.

item.title: AI Roll-Ups: Buy a Boring Business, Run It with Agents
item.description:
Greg Isenberg's X article makes the case for AI roll-ups: buy an established services business and run its back office with AI agents.
His playbook: buy the customers and trust, build a rulebook and review checkpoints, and move margins from 5-10% toward 30-40%.
Guests add balance: even Thrive needed more than off-the-shelf AI, and AI users get less accurate when they stop checking.
Sources: - $5T opportunity: AI Roll Ups, GREG ISENBERG (@gregisenberg) (https://x.com/gregisenberg/status/2103927365977928019) - The Revolution in Services: General Catalyst's AI Rollup Strategy, with Marc Bhargava, Nathan Labenz (https://www.cognitiverevolution.ai/the-revolution-in-services-general-catalysts-ai-rollup-strategy-with-marc-bhargava) - OpenAI hopes to automate IT and accounting with Thrive Holdings, Nicole Kobie (https://www.itpro.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/openai-hopes-to-automate-it-and-accounting-with-thrive-holdings) - Centaurs and Cyborgs on the Jagged Frontier, Ethan Mollick (https://www.oneusefulthing.org/p/centaurs-and-cyborgs-on-the-jagged)

item.title: Why Software Factories Fail: The Harness Is Not Enough
item.description:
Dex Horthy's X article, part one of Why Software Factories Fail, argues the lights-off software factory does not work.
Coding models are trained to pass tests, and there is no penalty for eroding codebase maintainability.
Guests add DORA and METR data on delivery stability and developer speed, plus how SWE-bench tasks are graded.
Sources: - Why Software Factories Fail, dex (@dexhorthy) (https://x.com/dexhorthy/status/2080697380379427275) - SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?, Carlos E. item.title: Your Old Prompts Are Making Claude Worse: Cheaper, Better Claude

item.title: The most lucrative AI business to start in 2027
item.description:

item.title: The road to self-improving software
item.description:
An X article by Ben Holmes on building a closed-loop software factory with agents.
Agents can proactively fix alerted bugs, score their own sessions to improve skills, and mine customer data for the roadmap.
It shifts the goal from faster pull requests to one loop from task to shipped product, with humans still reviewing.
